headline: Your Ezoic waterfall journey.
subheadline: A scrollable GTMx strategy artifact for routing independent publishers into the right Ezoic monetization offer. List building, campaign angles, and sample copy, prepared for Mike McGuire. First campaign on us.
productSummary: Ezoic is a publisher monetization platform: AI optimization, first-party identity (ezID), premium demand, video, and Core Web Vitals-friendly ad delivery on the publisher's own domain. No upfront cost. Ezoic earns a share when the publisher earns. The homepage also sells performance advertising to brands. This playbook does not mix that advertiser motion into the waterfall.
coreInsight: Eva already opened on digital publishers who want more ad revenue and a better audience experience. That is still the live product at ezoic.com/publishers and ezoic.com/monetize. The one TAM is independent publishers and video platforms. The one routing signal is the public ad stack (ads.txt plus BuiltWith), because it is observable without paid enrichment and it tells you whether they are trapped on a premium network, running AdSense, sitting on unused first-party data, or not monetizing yet.

sections.label: Signal
sections.title: The signal is the public ad stack
sections.takeaway: A publisher's ads.txt file and detected ad tech show who already takes a cut of their inventory. That is stronger than a traffic guess, and it is free to collect.

sections.label: Waterfall
sections.title: One cascade routes every publisher
sections.takeaway: First match wins. Premium competitor networks go first, then AdSense and header bidding, then first-party or video inventory, then everyone else.

sections.label: Tiers
sections.title: Each stack gets a different first offer
sections.takeaway: Switchers get a network teardown. AdSense sites get a lift brief. List- and video-led sites get a first-party or UX note. The rest get a no-upfront-cost starter.

sections.label: Campaigns
sections.title: Eva's three angles, mapped onto the waterfall
sections.takeaway: The list is always publishers and monetization leaders. Personalization and the revenue-versus-engagement A/B sit on top of the same exclusive routes. They are not a second TAM.

sections.label: Email Copy
sections.title: Copy that names the stack they already run
sections.takeaway: Notice the ads.txt partner or the empty inventory, poke the revenue or UX bind that stack creates, then ask for a one-letter yes.

sections.label: Launch
sections.title: Launch the switchers first, on us
sections.takeaway: GTMx funds the first campaign. Start with premium-network publishers, prove reply density, then roll AdSense, first-party, and the catch-all.

signalReasons: ads.txt is public, bulk-crawlable, and already names Mediavine, Raptive, AdThrive, Freestar, Google, and Ezoic as sellers.
BuiltWith and Wappalyzer confirm the same networks plus AdSense, Ad Manager, and Prebid when ads.txt is thin.
The signal maps to live Ezoic copy: keep the domain and the audience, put every impression into an auction, and use first-party identity instead of a walled garden.
Traffic tools can optionally qualify the TAM later. They are not required to route an account.

routingRules.if: remaining independent publisher or video platform in TAM

tiers.name: Tier 1
tiers.label: Premium network switch
tiers.trigger: ads.txt or BuiltWith shows Mediavine, Raptive, AdThrive, or Freestar
tiers.pain: A premium network already takes the inventory, so UX, first-party data, and yield sit inside someone else's rules. Switching feels risky even when the page is crowded and the audience file is unused.
tiers.valueProp: Ezoic keeps the publisher's domain, data, and audience, runs a real-time auction on every impression, and tunes layout per visitor. Direct brand campaigns stay on the page and the publisher keeps that revenue.
tiers.replyDensity: Highest intent. They already monetize at network scale.

tiers.name: Tier 2
tiers.label: Independent stack lift
tiers.trigger: AdSense, Google Ad Manager, or header bidding, and no premium competitor network
tiers.pain: Inventory is live, but it is not in a full auction with per-visitor testing. Yield and UX are both guesses.
tiers.valueProp: Ezoic puts premium demand on every impression, tests placements automatically, and measures session revenue rather than a single page RPM.
tiers.dataSource: ads.txt Google seller + BuiltWith AdSense / GAM / Prebid
tiers.replyDensity: Strong. Budget is already in ads. The stack is underpowered.

tiers.name: Tier 3
tiers.label: First-party and video
tiers.trigger: Login, newsletter, subscriber list, or a video player, and no premium network
tiers.pain: They already own an audience or video inventory, then monetize it like anonymous display. Advertisers pay more for identified users, and sticky video is the high-value unit, so both are leaking.
tiers.valueProp: ezID turns logins and lists into privacy-safe identity. Ezoic publishes 110%+ EPMV improvement for U.S. identified users. A player and video network are built in, on the publisher's domain.
tiers.dataSource: Site scrape for forms and players + ads.txt gap
tiers.replyDensity: Good. Personalize on the list or the player they already have.

tiers.name: Catch-all
tiers.label: Not monetizing yet
tiers.trigger: Every remaining independent publisher or video platform in the TAM
tiers.pain: The site has audience and no serious ad stack, so visits are unpaid and there is no test of whether ads can fund growth without wrecking UX.
tiers.valueProp: No upfront cost. A JS snippet or SDK, preview before going live, and Ezoic earns only when the publisher does.
tiers.dataSource: Publisher TAM scrape + LinkedIn titles, after higher tiers are routed out
tiers.replyDensity: Broadest coverage. Softest ask. Still 100% of TAM.

campaigns.name: Network Switch Teardown
campaigns.strategy: Name the ads.txt partner and contrast Ezoic's per-visitor auction plus publisher-owned data
campaigns.overview: Eva angle 1 + 3. Scrape publishers, write to the monetization lead, and lead with yield they do not control on the current network.

campaigns.name: UX versus network density
campaigns.filter: Same Tier 1 list, engagement copy instead of RPM copy
campaigns.strategy: Poke crowded placements and Core Web Vitals, then offer Ezoic Cloud plus per-visitor layout testing
campaigns.overview: A/B against the switch teardown. Same accounts, same exclusive route, engagement language instead of revenue language.

campaigns.name: Independent Stack Lift
campaigns.filter: AdSense, GAM, or Prebid, no premium network
campaigns.strategy: Name the current seller and show what a full auction plus Ad Tester changes
campaigns.overview: The AdSense and header-bidding majority. Revenue-growth side of Eva's A/B.

campaigns.name: Fewer ads, more pages
campaigns.strategy: Lead with session revenue and Ezoic's published 28% average visitor engagement lift
campaigns.overview: A/B against the lift brief. Same waterfall tier, UX-first hook.

campaigns.name: First-party and video brief
campaigns.filter: Newsletter, login, or video player detected
campaigns.strategy: Personalize on {{first_party_signal}} or {{video_signal}} and ezID / built-in video
campaigns.overview: Eva angle 2. This is where first-party benefits and UX improvements are the trigger, not a bolted-on paragraph.

campaigns.name: Publisher Starter Map
campaigns.filter: Remaining publishers and video platforms, no ad stack
campaigns.strategy: Notice the missing ads.txt, offer a no-upfront-cost starter map
campaigns.overview: Catch-all coverage so every scraped publisher still gets one route. Revenue-growth side of the A/B.

campaigns.name: Audience-first starter
campaigns.strategy: Lead with Leap / Ezoic Cloud, Core Web Vitals, and growing an owned audience before stacking ads
campaigns.overview: A/B against the starter map. Still exclusive catch-all, still one TAM.

But would it be fair to assume yield, layout, and the audience file now sit inside {{ad_network}}'s rules, so {{company_name}} cannot test a different auction without a full network move?

Ezoic keeps your domain, your data, and your audience, then runs a real-time auction on every impression and tunes placements per visitor. Direct brand campaigns stay on the page and you keep that revenue.

Reply Y and I'll send a Network Switch Teardown for {{site_name}}, your current seller list against an Ezoic-style auction. No call needed.

{{first_name}}, the part that usually gets ignored is not the RPM screenshot. It is the UX tax.

Networks optimize for their package. Ezoic tests layout per visitor and can serve ads from the edge with the page, which is the Core Web Vitals path their Cloud product is built for.

Want the Network Switch Teardown for {{site_name}}? Reply Y.

launchPlan: Scrape independent publishers and video platforms, pull ads.txt, and exclude any domain that already lists Ezoic as a seller.
Resolve CMO / Head of Monetization / publisher-revenue titles only after the domain is routed. First campaign is on GTMx.
Launch Tier 1 Network Switch first. Smallest list, sharpest signal, revenue copy as the control.
A/B the UX / engagement variant on the same Tier 1 list once the control has a read, not as a separate TAM.
Add Tier 2 AdSense lift, then Tier 3 first-party and video, then the catch-all starter so coverage stays at 100%.

thresholds.rate: Dense positive replies on the first pass
thresholds.action: Scale that tier. Keep the winning revenue or engagement variant.

thresholds.rate: Steady replies, no clear winner yet
thresholds.action: Let it run. Do not mix advertiser-demand copy into this TAM.

thresholds.rate: Thin replies after a full first pass
thresholds.action: Swap only the lead magnet or the first-line stack mention. Do not change the route.

thresholds.rate: No density after a full pass of the tier
thresholds.action: Cut that copy variant. Keep the exclusive waterfall.
